Social Structures and Inequality.Economic Inequality: Empirical studies on wealth, income, and resource distribution using surveys, panel data, experiments, and field interventions.
Social Structures and Inequality.Race and Ethnicity: Experimental and observational research on social stratification, discrimination, and identity; often involves survey experiments, lab-in-the-field studies, and longitudinal datasets.
Social Structures and Inequality.Gender and Sexuality: Studies using experiments, surveys, and observational methods to investigate gender norms, roles, and disparities.

Social Behavior and Interactions.Social Networks: Empirical analysis of relationships and interactions using network surveys, behavioral experiments, and digital trace data.
Social Behavior and Interactions.Group Behavior and Cooperation: Lab and field experiments on trust, cooperation, collective action, and coordination.
Social Behavior and Interactions.Deviance and Crime: Empirical work on criminal behavior, policing, and social control using field experiments, natural experiments, and longitudinal datasets.

Organizations and Institutions.Education Systems: Experimental and quasi-experimental studies on schooling outcomes, educational interventions, and policy impacts.
Organizations and Institutions.Work and Labor Organizations: Empirical research on organizational behavior, labor markets, and productivity using field experiments and observational data.
Organizations and Institutions.Political and Legal Institutions: Field and survey experiments examining governance, voting behavior, policy compliance, and institutional effectiveness.

Culture and Communication.Media and Information: Empirical studies on communication, media consumption, misinformation, and social influence using experiments and surveys.
Culture and Communication.Norms and Cultural Values: Experimental and observational studies on cultural attitudes, moral norms, and behavioral change.

Cultural Anthropology.Ethnographic Field Studies: Systematic observation, interviews, and participatory research to document contemporary cultural practices.
Cultural Anthropology.Experimental Cultural Psychology: Field and lab experiments investigating cognition, social behavior, and cultural variation in behavior and norms.

Biological and Evolutionary Anthropology.Human Evolution and Paleobiology: Empirical research on fossils, comparative anatomy, and experimental studies simulating evolutionary processes.
Biological and Evolutionary Anthropology.Human Biological Variation: Population studies measuring genetics, physiology, health, and adaptation; often includes field experiments or controlled laboratory measurements.

Archaeology.Field Excavation and Survey: Systematic excavation, site survey, and artifact analysis with experimental validation of dating and provenance.
Archaeology.Experimental Archaeology: Reconstruction and testing of past technologies and practices to understand artifact function, material properties, and social behavior.

Linguistic Anthropology.Language and Cognition: Empirical studies on language acquisition, multilingualism, and cognitive effects of linguistic structures, using field and lab experiments.
Linguistic Anthropology.Sociolinguistics and Dialects: Quantitative and experimental studies of language variation, social signaling, and communication patterns.

Applied Anthropology.Public Health and Medical Anthropology: Field experiments and observational studies on health interventions, disease transmission, and culturally informed health behaviors.
Applied Anthropology.Environmental and Ecological Anthropolog: Empirical studies on human-environment interactions, resource use, and conservation practices using field measurements and participatory research.
